FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 20 February 1989, after the 
draft finalized by the Dye Intermediates Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, 
Coal and Related Products Division Council. 



6-Chloro-2-aminophenol-4-sulphonic acid ( CgHjOjNSCl ) is 
dyes. It is represented by the following structural formula: 



used as an intermediate for reactive 




SOjH 



6-Chloro-2-Aminophenol-4-Sulphonic Acid 

{ Molecular Mass 223" 5 ) 

CAS Registry Number [ 5857-94-3 ] 

Requirement of assay, matter insoluble in sodium carbonate solution and isomeric impurity, namely, 
4-chloro-2-aminophenol-6-sulphonic acid have been stipulated in this standard. However, the 
committee at the time of preparation of this standard, envisaged to incorporate the requirement of 
other impurities also as and when the same are identified and details of their test methods are 
available. 



For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the 
final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS 2:1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revwerf)'. The number of 
significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value 
in this standard.

6-CHLORO-2-AMINOPHENOL- 

4-SULPHONIC ACID, TECHNICAL — 

SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard prescribes the requirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for 6-chloro-2- 
aminophenol-4-sulphonic acid, technical, 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard. 



IS No. 
IS 1070 : 1977 

IS 2552 : 1979 

IS 5299 : 1969 



Title 

Specification for water for 
general laboratory use ( second 
revision ) 

Specification for steel drums 
( galvanized and ungalva- 
nized ) ( second revision ) 

Methods of sampling and tests 
for dye intermediates 



3 REQjUIREMENTS 

3.1 Description 

The material shall be dry or in the form of paste 
and yellowish brown to greyish brown in colour. 

3.2 The material shall also comply with require- 
ments given in Table I. 

4 PACKING AND MARKING 

4.1 Packing 

The material shall be packed in HDPE bags, jute 
bags with polyethylene liner, paper bags or steel 
drums ( see IS 2552 : 1979 ) lined with suitable 
polyethylene film or as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier. Each container shall 
be securely closed. 

4.2 Marking 

Each container shall bear legibly and indelibly the 



following information: 

a) Name of the material; 

b) Name of the manufacturer and his recog- 
nized trade-mark, if any; 

c) Batch number; and 

d) Gross, net and tare mass. 

5 SAMPLING 

The material shall be sampled in accordance with 
3 of IS 5299 : 1969. 

6 TEST METHODS 

6.1 Tests shall be carried out according to the 
methods prescribed in Annex A, as indicated in 
col 4 of the Table 1. 

6.2 Qiiality of Reagents 

Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and 
distilled water {see IS 1070: 1977) shall be 
employed in tests. 

NOTE — 'Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that 
do not contain impurities which affect the resuhs of 
analysis.

ANNEX A 
( Clause 61 i and Table 1 ) 

METHOD OF TEST FOR 
6-CHLORO-2-AMINOPHENOL-4-SULPHONIC ACID, TECHNICAL 

A-0 PREPARED SAMPLE 



A-0.1 Dry the material at 105 ± 1°C to constant 
mass. Grind and mix well. Transfer the material 
to a wide-mouthed bottle and stopper it. Do not 
expose the sample to an atmosphere containing 
acidic or alkaline fumes. Use this prepared 
sample for tests. 

A-1 DETERMINATION OF MATTER 
INSOLUBLE IN SODIUM CARBONATE 
SOLUTION 

A-1.1 Reagent 

A-l.l.l Sodium Carbonate Solution, 10 percent 
(m/v). 

A- 1.2 Apparatus 

A-1.2.1 Beaker, 1 000-ml. 

A- 1.2.2 Sintered Glass Crucible, Ga. 

A-1.3 Procedure 

Weigh accurately about 20 g of prepared sample 
( A-0.1 ) and transfer into a 1 000-ml beaker. Add 
60 ml of water followed by sodium carbonate 
solution till it is faint alkaline to brilliant yellow 
paper. Heat to dissolve completely. Filter hot 
through sintered glass crucible and wash with hot 
water till free from alkali. Preserve the filtrate 
and washings for assay as given in A-2. Dry the 
residue at 100°C to a constant mass. 

A-1.4 Calculation 



Matter insoluble in 
sodium carbonate 
solution, percent 
by mass 



M 



X 109 



where 
Mi=mass in g of sintered crucible with 
residue, 

A/g^niass in g of empty sintered crucible, 
and 

M =mass in g of sample taken for test. 

A-2 ASSAY 

A-2.1 Reagents 

A-2.1.1 Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid 

A-2. 1.2 Sodium Nitrite Solution, N/10. 

A-2.2 Procedure 

Cool the filtrate and washings ( A-L3 ) to room 
temperature. Dilute with water to I 000 ml in a 



volumetric flask and mix well. Pipette out 100 ml 
aliquot in 1 000-ml beaker. Add 400 ml ice-cold 
water followed by 35 ml of concentrated hydro ■ 
chloric acid. Titrate with N/10 sodium nitrite 
solution at 15°C, while stirring mechanically, 
using potassium starch iodide papers to a 5 minute 
end point. 



A-2.3 Calculation 

Assay, percent by mass 



F X AT X 223-5 
M 



where 
V = volume of N/10 sodium nitrite solution 
required, 

N == normality of sodium nitrite solution, 
and 

M = mass in g of sample taken for test. 

A-3 DETERMINATION OF 4-GHLORO-2- 
AMINOPHENOL.6-SULPHONIG ACID 

A-3.0 Outline of the Method 

4-Chloro-2-aminophenol-6-sulphonic acid content 
is estimated by ascending thin layer chromato- 
graphic separation on cellulose MN 300 plate. 

A-3.1 Apparatus 

A-3.1.1 Chromatographic Chamber, 220 x 100 x 
220 mm. 

A-3. 1.2 Micro Pipette, 10 /xl capacity. 

A-3.1.3 Thin Layer Chromatographic Glass Plate, 
200 X 200 mm. 

A-3.1.4 Adjustable Thin Plate Applicator 

A-3.1.5 Chromatographic Spray Bottle 

A-3. 1.6 Oven with Thermo Regulator 

A-3.2 Reagents 

A-3.2.1 Solution of 4-Chloro-2-Aminophenol- 
6-Sulphonic Acid, 0005 percent in 1 percent 
ammonia on 100 percent basis. 

A-3.2.2 Eluent, «-propanol : benzene : 5 percent 
ammonia ( 70 : 10 : 30 ) ( v/v ). 

A-3.2.3 Sodium Nitrite Solution, 1 N. 

A-3.2.4 Hydrocholic Acid, 1 N. 

A-3.2.5 Spray Reagent, 05 percent solution of 
alpha-naphthol in ehtanolic soda ash solution 
( 5 percent ) ( 1 : 1 ). 

A-3.2.6 Cellulose MN 300 Powder 



IS 12618 : 1989 



A-3.3 Procedure 

A-3.3.1 Preparation of Chromatographic Plate 

Mix 150 g of cellulose MN 300 with 90 to 100 
ml water for 10 minutes. Then by means of 
applicator, coat the plate with cellulose MN layer 
of thickness not exceeding 5 mm and place it 
in oven maintained at 110°C for 90 minutes. By 
means of a needle, mark a thin line widthwise on 
all plates at about 30 mm from the upper edge. 
Also remove a band of about 5 mm width 
cellulose MN from either of the lateral sides of 
each plate. 

A-3.3.2 Preparation of the Solution 

Homogenize the sample for a few minutes and 
weigh by means of a weighing bottle I'O g ( 100 
percent basis ) of the material and transfer to a 
100-ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in 1 percent 
ammonia solution and make up the solution to 
mark, by adding additional quantity of 1 percent 
ammonia solution. 



A-3.3.3 Chromatographic Separation 

Pipette out 10 /»1 of (he sample solution 
( A-3.3.2 ) and 10 /*1 of the reference solution 
( A-3.2.1 ) in the form of a uniform line on the 
plate at a distance of 30 mm from the bottom 
edge. After complete evaporation of the solvent, 
place the plate in the chromatographic chamber 
and allow the eluent ( A-3.2.2 ) in the chamber to 
migrate for about 1 50 mm. When it reaches the 
upper line of the plate, remove the plate and let 
it dry in air for at least 30 minutes. Dry the 
place completely. Diazotize in nitrous [IN 
NaNOg + 1 N HCL (1 : 2 ) ( v/v ) ] and couple 
with spray reagent ( A-3.2.5 ) by spraying. Let 
the plate stand for at least ] 5 minutes. 

A-3.3.4 Evaluation 

By visual comparison, the spot corresponding to 
4-chloro-2-aminophenol-6-sulphonic acid of the 
sample shall have equal or less intensity than that 
of the reference sample corresponding to 0'5 per- 
cent of 4-chloro-2-aminophenol-6-sulphonic acid. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards.
